scope.title: Cross-cutting entities, buildings, world objects, events, shared state, and lifecycle archaeology
scope.objective: Recover relationship-first abstractions that cut across Cell, Creature/Tribe/Civilization, Space, editor, UI, and animation modes without flattening mode-specific records into an invented universal entity or event ABI.
included: Generic refcounted, serializable, game-data, spatial, noun, and world-object relationships
Cell pooled objects and Cell world state as a mode-specific comparison
City, building, building-data, layout-slot, and building-subtype relationships where evidenced
App messages, mode messages, animation events, deferred events, feedback events, communication events, and mode-specific event records
Creation, lookup, mutation, update, serialization, destruction, and ownership paths
Ten unnamed high-fan-in Simulator shared-state roots and map_int_whatever_find
OpenSpore source comparison and reconstruction-package boundaries
excluded: Detailed proprietary file-format parsing beyond identity and ownership relationships
Any proprietary EA source, asset, model, texture, sound, or script
Ghidra mutation, renaming, typing, bookmarking, saving, or program exit
Claims of runtime verification without a runtime trace

claim_policy.current_source_role: comparison only; current types and behavior do not backfill original semantics
claim_policy.sdk_role: name, structure, vtable, and method-surface evidence; not standalone body or ownership proof
claim_policy.address_rule: An SDK label at a non-function or mismatched function boundary is retained as an SDK anchor but is not treated as an exact function body.
claim_policy.inheritance_rule: Common prefixes, vtables, and field reuse are recorded as structural relationships; SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI, so C++ inheritance is only promoted when SDK declarations and repeated structure support it.

evidence_scale.label: VERIFIED
evidence_scale.meaning: Directly read from a pinned binary/export artifact or exact current repository record; not runtime-verified unless explicitly stated.

evidence_scale.label: CONFIRMED
evidence_scale.meaning: Direct targeted static body plus corroborating structure, xref, or second source; still not runtime-verified.

evidence_scale.label: SUPPORTED
evidence_scale.meaning: Static structure, vtable, committed dossier, or multi-source agreement supports the bounded claim.

evidence_scale.label: INFERRED
evidence_scale.meaning: A semantic interpretation follows from names, layout, call shape, or repeated use, with material uncertainty retained.

evidence_scale.label: OBSERVED
evidence_scale.meaning: Literal current OpenSpore source behavior; comparison-only for the original.

evidence_scale.label: APPROXIMATION
evidence_scale.meaning: A usable clean-room value or behavior with known material divergence from the original.

evidence_scale.label: UNKNOWN
evidence_scale.meaning: The available evidence does not establish the claim.

relationships.meaning: The original has a tiny universal refcount/Cast root and a separate Simulator serialization interface layered onto game-data-like objects.
cGameData adds noun identity, owner, political identity, view/scenario membership, and list links to the serialization interface.
Noun instances are linked into intrusive noun lists and indexed by noun/definition/political IDs; the manager is the broadest recovered instance factory and materializer.
These families share serializable game-data identity, but add distinct spatial, behavior, naming, locomotion, or orbital state.
relationships.limit: No MSVC RTTI is present; do not infer additional direct base classes beyond SDK declarations.

relationships.relation: secondary spatial vtable and transform/model state
relationships.meaning: Spatial state is a reusable mixin rather than the universal object root.
The city keeps intrusive building references and layout state; each building can point to owner city and carries noun/political identity.
Slots retain intrusive cGameData references and positions; city building vectors and layout slots are related but separate representations.
The city data record contains building/ornament/wall value vectors and economy/capture state; this is not the live intrusive object graph.
Cell entities are pool-indexed records owned by one stage state object, not cGameData instances.
One pooled object is reachable by pool index, spatial query, GFX association, resource key, and animation/health state.
A message ID selects listener or callback entries; payloads may be unmanaged, refcounted, or function-posted and are released at queue/listener boundaries.
Communication events retain source/target city/civilization pointers, mission/dialog identity, timing, priority, and serializable response vectors.
Feedback records have their own display/lifetime semantics and are not App StandardMessages.

persistence.conclusion: Persistence is layered rather than a single entity save format: serializable game-data interfaces, a class/property serializer, mode-specific serializable records, a central persistence service, and DBPF/resource storage all participate. App messages and most domain event records are runtime dispatch values, not save records.

persistence.serializable_exception: cCommEvent is both a runtime communication record and an ISimulatorSerializable object; it must retain both dispatch-lifetime and persistence relationships.
persistence.openspore_gap: Current OpenSpore has typed asset readers, declarative scene JSON, deterministic stateString/manifests, and tests, but no general cGameData/noun save-load, cCellSerializableData codec, property round-trip, cGamePersistenceManager equivalent, or runtime save/load integration.

openspore_comparison.conclusion: OpenSpore has useful mode and Cell-local abstractions, but it does not yet implement the original cross-mode object graph. Its strongest reusable ideas are typed handles/indices, deterministic lifecycle, a Cell object pool, world references, a scene identity value, and a local event record. Its main missing layer is a semantic registry/owner/message/persistence spine connecting Cell, Creature/Tribe/Civilization, Space, and editor modes.

recommended_semantic_mapping.modern_role: EntityHandle plus explicit owner, stable ID, definition ID, political ID, lifetime, and persistence metadata
recommended_semantic_mapping.rule: Do not reproduce vtable layout unless compatibility requires it; do not force Cell pooled records into this interface.

recommended_semantic_mapping.modern_role: IObjectRegistry and IObjectFactory with definition-to-instance materialization
recommended_semantic_mapping.rule: Keep live owner graphs, maps, and vectors separate; provide stable handles and explicit enumeration.

recommended_semantic_mapping.modern_role: WorldObjectState with transform, bounds, model identity, visibility, and interaction flags
recommended_semantic_mapping.rule: Use per-mode adapters; orbital bodies, creatures, buildings, and Cell objects have different state domains.

recommended_semantic_mapping.modern_role: CityState, BuildingState, and BuildingSlot with explicit owner and placement relationships
recommended_semantic_mapping.rule: Keep live objects separate from cCityData/cBuildingData save-value records.

recommended_semantic_mapping.modern_role: IEventRouter with typed EventEnvelope, registration handles, deterministic ordering, and explicit ownership
recommended_semantic_mapping.rule: Use mode/domain event variants; do not create one universal original event ABI.

recommended_semantic_mapping.modern_role: IStateStore with versioned object snapshots and explicit migrations
recommended_semantic_mapping.rule: Preserve stable IDs and save semantics, not original codec implementation.

openspore_comparison.integration_warning: Current CellGame/pool/query/advect/combat components are documented as not integrated into the CellSim frame loop; current CellSim entities and CellGame pooled objects therefore remain parallel projections.

contradictions.issue: Several SDK function addresses are labels at or inside current Ghidra function boundaries rather than exact entries.
examples: cGameNounManager::CreateInstance at 0x00b20bf0 versus nearby factory mechanics at 0x00b20c60
cGameNounManager::DestroyInstance at 0x00b22560 inside/ending the 0x00b22440 cleanup body
cObjectPool_::Initialize at 0x00b72190 versus allocation/reset mechanics at 0x00b72160
cMessageManager::MessageSend at 0x008854a0 with no exact current function entry
cGameData::Write at 0x00b184d0 inside the 0x00b184c0 destructor-like body
ClassSerializer::Write at 0x006928c0 inside the 0x00692880 attribute-initialization body
contradictions.resolution: Preserve SDK names and addresses as SDK anchors; attach body claims only to exact current functions or mechanics-only regions with explicit limits.

contradictions.issue: The old dossier called FUN_00b21340 message-handler registration, while current static mechanics show a noun map/list callback and materialization bridge.
contradictions.resolution: The noun-map/list interpretation supersedes the message-handler label; exact cGameNounManager method identity remains unclaimed.

contradictions.issue: cGameNounManager::GetData at 0x00b212d0 and FUN_00b21340 are adjacent but distinct current functions, while older notes discussed them as one method identity.
contradictions.resolution: Keep the exact SDK-named GetData function and the mechanics-only adjacent bridge separate.

contradictions.issue: map_int_whatever_find is named as a find helper but performs unsigned lower_bound and can return a greater key or end.
contradictions.resolution: Use map_uint_lower_bound as a reconstruction role; preserve the existing address/name in provenance and require callers to perform equality checks where needed.

contradictions.issue: FUN_00b1fdb0 is consumed as both scalar/action-handle-like and pointer-like object with vtable-style field access.
contradictions.resolution: Keep the return opaque and do not assign player-ID, object-pointer, or service-manager type without new evidence.

contradictions.issue: FUN_00b3d300 and FUN_00b3d2a0 have very high fan-in but many callers discard their return values.
contradictions.resolution: Do not model every call as acquiring a service object; preserve read-only slot and optional-use semantics.

contradictions.issue: The 0x14-byte IMessageManager::Entry is registration/listener metadata, while ProcessQueue traverses distinct 0x18-byte records.
contradictions.resolution: Model registration entries and queued records as different schemas.

contradictions.issue: The 0x0F43029A world-object record name resembles a runtime world-object class, but committed evidence identifies it as a model-group asset record without placement/ownership.
contradictions.resolution: Keep it in asset_types and do not derive cBuilding, cGameData, or scene placement from it.

contradictions.issue: SDK IGameMode slot order, recovered concrete cCellModeStrategy slots, and current OpenSpore IGameMode comments are not one universal ABI.
contradictions.resolution: Compare lifecycle semantics, not raw slot numbers, and keep original/concrete/current orders separate.

contradictions.issue: Current OpenSpore has two parallel Cell representations: CellSim role/value entities and CellGame pooled cCellObjectData state, but they are not integrated in the frame loop.
contradictions.resolution: Do not claim current OpenSpore implements the original cCellObjectData lifecycle end to end; treat both as bounded comparison projections.

contradictions.issue: cGameData and cSpatialObject/common-prefix layouts support a broad object family, but SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI.
contradictions.resolution: Record SDK-declared and structural relationships while withholding claims about unobserved direct bases or virtual inheritance layout.
